title: a-counting-learning-block-predicts-who-writes-what-from-the-artifact-journal
author: CC
from_idea: none, because it is the second follow-on named verbatim in ticket 30531f6e1c5d's follow_ons field (CairnCommons/tickets/30531f6e1c5d-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json), born of the Friston free-energy text Akien brought on 2026-09-13 and captured in CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-13-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json ('an alternative to LLM ... to perform inspections')

owning_intention: cairn/machines/counting_block/intention+why.json (to be written beside the code at BUILDME)
pre_approval: Akien, 2026-09-13, on the parent ticket: 'approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH' — the ruling names both follow-ons; the parent's cast recorded them as cast 'when this ticket reaches PROVEME'. Pre-approval of THIS build is not claimed: it stands at his review queue.
intention: A counting learning block over the artifact journal predicts who writes what (a frequency table over path-class × verb × caller-class) and raises only the entry outside the table, so the inspection of record writes is arithmetic that runs on every append and the LLM is spent only when the table itself must change.
why: the intention I-the-system-is-a-learning-block.md (spanning; the block anatomy: a door, a prior, an error signal, a local adjustment) and learns-its-gates (the system learns its gates from evidence); Law 1 (the resolver spent on the novel — a triple seen 400 times is settled, only the unseen one costs attention); Law 3 (the table is measured from the journal, never authored)
how: A tenant of the learning-block anatomy: compile a count table over (path class, verb, caller class) from both artifact journals; on the door's probe poke, a zero-count triple raises one trouble through the trouble device; an akien-class clearance increments the row, a cc-class clearance does not; the first measurement is compression (rows << entries).
how_first_cut: Under cairn/machines/learning_block's existing anatomy (the charter cairn-machines-learning_block--intention+why.json): (1) the table — counts of (path class from jurisdiction.json, verb, caller class) compiled from both .artifact-journal.jsonl files, kept in instance-space under the holder that assembled it (Law 6 — a tool's state berths under its holder); (2) the prediction — for a new entry, its (class, verb, caller) frequency; (3) the error — an entry whose triple has count zero, or whose caller class is unknown, raised as a trouble through the trouble device with the entry and the table row; (4) the local adjustment — a raised entry that Akien clears increments the table (the world was right, the prior was wrong); (5) the trigger is the door's existing probe poke (callers_are_known already runs after every append) — no poller, no daemon (memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll). Friston's loop is cited, not grafted: prediction = frequency, free energy = surprise of the triple, action = raise, learning = the count.
falsifier: DONE when, measured by cairn/machines/<block>/proofs/: (1) the table compiles from both journals and is reproducible from them alone — delete it, recompile, byte-identical; (2) a seeded journal entry with an unseen triple raises exactly one trouble naming the triple and the row; a seen triple raises nothing; (3) an akien-class clearance increments the row so the same triple no longer raises, and a cc-class clearance does not; (4) the block runs on the door's probe poke with no process of its own between appends (ps shows nothing; the poke is the only entry point); (5) over the live corpus the row count is well under the entry count (compression exists). WRONG INTENT if after 500 appends the table has one row per entry, or if the raise rate does not fall as rows fill — then the triple is the wrong prior and the block routes back to Akien with the table. HORIZON: the compression measurement is the first piece; if it reds, the ticket routes back before any raise is wired.

watchme.nexus: the who-writes-what tree — this block IS its first learner; the verdict teaches whether the triple is the right prior.

cast_checks.assumption_check: THREE, with standing. (1) That the triple (path class from jurisdiction.json, verb, caller class) is the right granularity — coarse enough to compress into few rows with high counts, fine enough that a gate writing a hand-edit or cc writing a seal is a zero-count row. UNMEASURED; measured at the first piece by compiling the table from the 1,326 genesis entries plus today's writes and reading the row count against the entry count (the falsifier's WRONG-INTENT clause: one row per entry means no compression). (2) That the door's probe poke is a usable trigger for a second consumer. MEASURED 2026-09-13: callers_are_known runs after every append (tooth test_the_probe_is_armed_with_carry_and_enough), so the poke exists; whether the door can carry two probes without a registry is decided at BUILDME's second piece — the cheapest shape is one probe module that calls the block, not a registry. (3) That cairn/machines/learning_block's anatomy fits a table-and-count tenant. Its charter (cairn-machines-learning_block--intention+why.json) is the prior art; read at BUILDME, and if its door demands an LLM-shaped prior the block is a NEW machine beside it and this cast's node_class stays code-seam either way.
cast_checks.missing_check: TWO points asserted wrapped that are not. (a) WHO CLEARS a raised triple: the trouble device owns raising and clearing, and a cleared trouble increments the row — but 'cleared by whom' matters: cc clearing its own novel write teaches the table that cc's novelty is normal. The cast records the answer: only a clearance whose caller class (read by the same door) is akien increments the table; a cc clearance retires the trouble and leaves the count at zero. Recorded on the ticket; the proof carries a tooth for it. (b) Laplace smoothing vs zero-count: a hard zero raises on the first write of every new component's state.json (a new class × append × gate row). That is CORRECT on day one (a new component is news) and noise by day thirty. The cast records the first shape as hard-zero with the smoothing parameter as the one knob the LLM adjusts (memory sieves-measure-not-judge), and the WATCHME measures whether the raise rate falls.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: DONE when, measured by cairn/machines/<block>/proofs/: (1) the table compiles from both journals and is reproducible from them alone — delete it, recompile, byte-identical; (2) a seeded journal entry with an unseen triple raises exactly one trouble naming the triple and the row; a seen triple raises nothing; (3) an akien-class clearance increments the row so the same triple no longer raises, and a cc-class clearance does not; (4) the block runs on the door's probe poke with no process of its own between appends (ps shows nothing; the poke is the only entry point); (5) over the live corpus the row count is well under the entry count (compression exists). WRONG INTENT if after 500 appends the table has one row per entry, or if the raise rate does not fall as rows fill — then the triple is the wrong prior and the block routes back to Akien with the table. HORIZON: the compression measurement is the first piece; if it reds, the ticket routes back before any raise is wired.
cast_checks.collision_check: Judged over the whys. Law 6: the table is DERIVED from the journal and reproducible, so it is instance-space state of the block's holder, not a record of truth — it does not go through the artifact door (jurisdiction.json's not_records already says derived surfaces are not records); a distinction recorded. The trouble device already owns raising/clearing; the block only feeds it — no second raiser. The corrosion sieve (constraint_enforcement_holds) is the same expected-vs-seen shape over a HAND-AUTHORED set; this block's set is measured, which is the difference Law 3 asks for — kin, not collision. memory ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat: the block adds nothing to the ground loop; it rides the door's poke. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
cast_checks.builder_check: A Haiku-level builder needs, and the ticket's how carries: (1) The table's shape: {(path_class, verb, caller_class): count}, path_class = the jurisdiction rule that matched (e.g. 'CairnCommons/tickets', 'cairn/state.json'), persisted as JSON under ~/.cairn/devices/<holder>/0/machines/<block>/table.json with the journal line counts it was compiled to. (2) The compile: read both .artifact-journal.jsonl from line 0, count triples; incremental on poke (append the new entry's triple). (3) The raise: trouble device's existing raise verb with evidence = the entry (path, verb, caller cgroup, at) and the row (count 0); one trouble per triple, deduped by triple. (4) The clear: on the trouble device's clear, read the clearer's class through artifact.caller(); akien increments, cc does not. (5) The trigger: the door's probe poke — build ONE probe module that calls the block, at cairn/machines/<block>/probes/raise_rate_falls.py, with trigger/carry/enough as probe.py demands. (6) The proof: a scratch pair of journals under set_diagnostic_roots, seeded triples, the trouble device pointed at a scratch store — the pattern test_artifact_door already uses.

decisions.text: THE POKE IS THE BEAT (2026-09-17, CC). The how says the block runs 'on the door's probe poke'; the artifact door has no probe-poke registry a second consumer can hook, and building one would be a registry for exactly two consumers. The beat's pulse service already calls every discovered groundloop/pulse.py after the probes (cairn/tools/base/shim.py _serve_pulses; discovery in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovery.py device_folders — device_id is the folder's parent name, so cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py is discovered as counting_block with no registration). So the poke the how names IS the beat: on_pulse(now, context) calls block.pulse(). No process, no poller, no registry — clause 4's ps shows nothing, and pulse_sites() lists the file. The beat stays the heartbeat and nothing more (memory ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat): this is a hook the beat calls, not a feature of the beat.

decisions.text: THE BLOCK RAISES THROUGH THE INHERITED EMISSION, NEVER THE TROUBLE DEVICE. The how says 'raises one trouble through the trouble device'; the machine_imports_no_device sieve (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py) reds any top-level cairn/machines/<name> file that imports cairn.devices.* (db_domain the one exemption; proofs/ and probes/ skipped, groundloop/ not). The sanctioned path is the ruling behind that sieve (Akien 2026-09-07: a trouble report is logging-shaped, so it sits in the basemost class): cairn.tools.base.diagnostic.ModuleRaiser('counting_block').raise_trouble(identity, why=..., detail=...) writes one raise_trouble emission into the block's own log home (instance/logs/counting_block/0/) and the trouble shim's drain (cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py drain -> _fold -> TroubleDevice.raise_trouble) folds it into one ticket per identity, counted. The identity is who-writes-what-<path class>-<verb>-<caller class>, so the second raise of a triple is the same trouble as the first. The proof (under proofs/, allowed to import the device) drives the shim's drain over a scratch instance root and a scratch store and asserts one ticket per identity with the count.

decisions.text: FULL FOLD PER BEAT, NOT INCREMENTAL. The two journals interleave by 'at' and an incremental fold of new lines would be order-unstable across the root boundary; the corpus is 2,675 entries on 2026-09-17 and a full compile is well under a second. compile(journals) is pure: ordered by (at, root name, line), arming = the first cairn-journal entry with path cairn/machines/counting_block/intention+why.json and verb genesis (position-based, so the arming entry itself is prior and everything after it is judged); a judged entry adds 1 to a nonzero row, and is a raise when the row is 0 (the row stays 0); a clear entry on troubles/who-writes-what-*.json by class akien adds 1 to the triple its slug names (read BEFORE the clear's own triple is counted), by any other class adds nothing and marks the raise cleared:<class>. Path class = the jurisdiction rule matched, spelled <root>/<under> | <root>/**/<parent> | <root>/**/<name>. Hard zero, no smoothing (cast missing_check (b)).

decisions.text: THREE FILES AT THE HOLDER'S ADDRESS, ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/counting_block/ (instance_path('cairn', 0) / 'machines' / 'counting_block'). table.json is the pure fold rendered with sort_keys and indent 1 — delete it, recompile, byte-identical (clause 1). raised.json is the ledger of journal lines already reported (root:line) — not part of the table because a record of what was SAID is not a measurement of what IS; delete it and the next beat re-reports onto the same identities, which the trouble device folds as recurrences (loud, never silent). probe_ack.json is {raises, bucket} from the PREVIOUS table (the first compile acks itself): the probe runs before the pulse modules on a beat, so it reads last beat's table against last beat's ack and fires exactly once per raise, on the beat after — every raise and every 100 post-arming appends, per the watchme, with no poller. The probe cairn/machines/counting_block/probes/raise_rate_falls.py reads only these files (never the journals — one reader of the corpus), carries rows, entries, raises per 200-append window, first vs last window rate, every raised triple with its disposition, and is ENOUGH at 1000 post-arming appends with last-window rate below first-window rate and at least one akien-class increment.

decisions.text: THE PULSE MODULE CONTRACT, SPELLED OUT (2026-09-17, CC; settles rehearsal pass 1's D1 read). cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py defines exactly one function, def on_pulse(now, context: dict | None = None) -> dict. It does not follow codemother's pulse pattern: it keeps no state of its own, writes no file of its own, has no first-run suppression, and fires on every beat including the first (the first compile acks itself, see the probe_ack line). Its whole body is out = block.pulse(now=now) and it returns {'block': 'counting_block', 'raised': <int, len(out['raised'])>, 'post_appends': <int>, 'compression': {'rows': int, 'entries': int, 'ratio': float}}. Every file it causes to be written is written by block.pulse() under instance_path('cairn', 0)/machines/counting_block/ (table.json, raised.json, probe_ack.json) — never beside the code. An exception propagating out of on_pulse is recorded by the pulse service as a refused hook and does not stop the beat.

decisions.text: THE TWO SMALL FILES' SCHEMAS, SPELLED OUT (2026-09-17, CC; settles pass 1's D4 read). raised.json is {'reported': [<str>, ...]} — a JSON object with the single key 'reported', a list of strings, each '<root>:<line>' (root is the journal root name 'cairn' or 'CairnCommons', line is the 1-based line number in that root's .artifact-journal.jsonl), one per journal entry already reported as a raise; on the live box today it reads {'reported': []}. probe_ack.json is {'raises': <int>, 'bucket': <int>} — raises is len(table['raises']) of the PREVIOUS beat's table (the total count of raise dispositions in the fold, not the delta), bucket is post_appends // 100 of the previous beat's table (post_appends = judged entries since arming); on the live box today it reads {'bucket': 0, 'raises': 0}. The probe's trigger is table['raises'] > ack['raises'] or table['post_appends'] // 100 > ack['bucket'], so it fires once on the beat after a raise or after a new 100-append bucket and is silent when the ack has caught up. Both are written atomically (tmp + os.replace) with json.dumps(sort_keys=True).

decisions.text: UNARMED MEANS EVERYTHING IS PRIOR AND NOTHING RAISES (2026-09-17, CC; settles pass 2's D3 read). arming_index(seq) walks the ordered stream for the first entry with root 'cairn', path 'cairn/machines/counting_block/intention+why.json' and verb 'genesis' and returns its position, or None when no such entry exists. compile() sets judged = armed is not None and i > armed, so with no arming entry every entry counts into its row as prior, raises is [], post_appends is 0, increments is [], and the table's 'armed' field is null; pulse() then writes the table and an empty ledger and reports nothing. The block is never armed by a timestamp, a config flag or the charter file's presence on disk — only by the genesis entry's position in the cairn journal — so a checkout with the charter file but without the journal line is unarmed, and a journal with the line but without the file is armed (the journal is the record of truth, Law 7).

Module-level PROVES = {'5a4ec289bf15': {'1': the_table_compiles_from_both_journals_and_is_byte_identical_when_recompiled, '2': an_unseen_triple_raises_exactly_one_trouble_and_a_seen_one_raises_nothing, '3': an_akien_clearance_teaches_the_row_and_a_cc_clearance_does_not, '4': the_block_runs_on_the_beat_with_no_process_of_its_own_and_the_probe_fires_once_per_raise, '5': over_the_live_corpus_rows_are_well_under_entries}} — the keys are proof_coverage.clauses(ticket) verbatim and each value is one tooth function name. A World class builds the scratch world: two temp journal roots named cairn and CairnCommons registered through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.set_diagnostic_roots({...}); entries hand-built with door._entry(rel, verb, why, before, after) then overridden for at and caller (so an akien-class entry exists, which no cc session can produce) and chained with door._append(root, entry); a scratch instance root passed as roots={'instance': ...} to ModuleRaiser and to cairn.devices.trouble.shim.TroubleShim(roots=..., root=<scratch CairnCommons/troubles>) whose drain() folds emissions into tickets; block.pulse(roots=..., raiser=..., where=<scratch table dir>) so no live file is touched. Teardown restores set_diagnostic_roots(None). A _tooth(name, fn) runner counts PASS/FAIL and prints each name; __main__ exits 1 on any FAIL. Tooth 5 alone reads the live journals, by home address (Path.home()/dev/src/{cairn,CairnCommons}/.artifact-journal.jsonl), and asserts invariants only (entries >= 500, rows*10 <= entries, unclassed == []), never a number. Tooth 4 monkeypatches block.table_dir and block.ModuleRaiser to the scratch world, asserts pulse_sites() lists the hook as counting_block, that ps shows no counting_block process other than the proof itself, and that the probe is silent-fires once-silent across three beats.

decisions.text: _Late IS DEFINED IN THE PROOF ITSELF (2026-09-17, CC; settles pass 4's D12 read). It is not a shared helper anywhere in the codebase; it is five lines at the top of cairn/machines/counting_block/proofs/test_counting_block.py: class _Late: def __init__(self, module): self._module = module; def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(importlib.import_module(self._module), name). Then block = _Late('cairn.machines.counting_block.block'), pulse_mod = _Late('cairn.machines.counting_block.groundloop.pulse'), probe_mod = _Late('cairn.machines.counting_block.probes.raise_rate_falls'). Every attribute access re-resolves the module through importlib, so nothing is imported until a tooth touches it and a reverted or missing build file raises inside that tooth (red) rather than at proof import (UNRAN under the hollow reading). The same shape appears in cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_no_direct_reach.py (50ad391f4e95, 2026-09-17) as precedent, not as an import.

decisions.text: THE PROBE, SPELLED OUT (2026-09-17, CC; settles pass 5's unlisted step and its read). cairn/machines/counting_block/probes/raise_rate_falls.py follows the precedent cairn/tools/artifact/probes/callers_are_known.py: a module-level PROBE = Probe(why=<str>, trigger=_trigger, to='harbor_master', body={'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}, carry=_carry, enough=_enough, horizon=1000) from cairn.tools.base.probe. It imports block (for table_dir, WINDOW=200, BUCKET=100) and nothing else of the system; ENOUGH_APPENDS = 1000. Helpers: _load(name) -> dict | None reads block.table_dir()/name; _measure(context) -> dict reads table.json and probe_ack.json once per beat into context {compiled: bool, raises: int, post_appends: int, windows: list[int] (raises per 200-append window), increments: list, rows: int, entries: int, raised: list, ack: {raises, bucket}}; _rates(context) -> (first, last) = raises-per-append over the first window and the last complete window, None when fewer than 200 post-arming appends. _trigger(now, context) -> bool is context['raises'] > ack['raises'] or context['post_appends'] // 100 > ack['bucket'] (False when the table is not compiled). _carry(context) -> dict returns {rows, entries, post_appends, raise_rate_per_window, first_window_rate, last_window_rate, increments, raised (first 50, each {identity, poke, root, line}), finding: <one of four sentences: not compiled / fewer than 200 appends / the rate FALLS (first -> last) / the rate does NOT fall — route back to Akien with the table>}. _enough(context) -> bool is post_appends >= 1000 and last < first and len(increments) >= 1. The probe reads only the block's three files, never the journals (one reader of the corpus). It carries no authority: it deposits and pokes; reopening the node is the owner's act (Law 6).

decisions.text: table.json's schema, READ OFF THE LIVE FILE 2026-09-24 (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/counting_block/table.json), eight top-level keys and no others: 'rows' — object mapping triple -> int count, the triple a single string '<path class>|<verb>|<caller class>' (e.g. 'CairnCommons/decisions|genesis|cc': 94); 'raises' — list of objects, each {at, caller_class, disposition ('raised' | 'cleared:akien' | 'cleared:cc' | 'cleared:<class>'), identity ('who-writes-what-<triple with | as ->'), identity_slug, line (int, 1-based journal line), path, post_append (int, this entry's position after arming), root ('cairn'|'CairnCommons'), row (int, the row's count when judged — 0 for a raise), triple, verb}; 'increments' — list of the akien clearances that added to a row, same entry shape; 'post_appends' — int, entries judged after arming; 'windows' — object mapping the WINDOW-sized bucket number as a string ('1', '5', ...) -> int raises in that bucket; 'unclassed' — list of entries no path class matched; 'armed' — {at, line, root} of the arming entry, or null when unarmed (D9); 'compiled_to' — object mapping root name -> int last journal line folded. Rendered by block.render: json.dumps(table, indent=1, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + newline. This settles D3's and D4's schema reads together.

decisions.text: The teeth's shape, READ OFF THE PROOF 2026-09-24: each tooth is a zero-argument module-level function named for its claim that returns nothing and signals red by raising — plain assert statements with a message, never try/except inside the tooth and never a bool return. The runner is _tooth(name, fn) in the proof: it calls fn(), counts PASS and prints '  green <name>' on a clean return, and on any Exception counts FAIL and prints '  RED   <name>: <ExcType>: <msg>'. TEETH is a module-level list of the tooth functions in order; __main__ runs _tooth(fn.__name__, fn) over TEETH inside try/finally (finally: door.set_diagnostic_roots(None) and rmtree of every _scratch dir), prints '<PASS> passed, <FAIL> failed out of <n>', and exits 1 if any failed.

SETTLES the two artifact-door seams D12 names (MEASURED 2026-09-24, cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py): set_diagnostic_roots(roots: dict[str, Path] | None) -> None (line 91) points the door at a scratch world — it maps root NAME ('cairn', 'CairnCommons') to a directory, resolves each path, and judges a scratch root by the live root's jurisdiction rules of the same name; None restores the live pair, which is the proof's teardown. _entry(rel, verb, why, before, after, *, count=1, extra=None) -> dict (line 313) builds one journal entry as a plain dict (it raises Refused for a verb not in VERBS) and writes nothing; the proof overrides that dict's 'at' and 'caller' keys and then chains it with _append(root: Path, entry: dict) -> dict (line 289), which appends under a lock. 'door' in D12 is the module cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.

MEASURED 2026-09-25: D3's path class already exists as a function: cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:85, path_class(root, rel, rules=None) -> str | None. It reads cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.jurisdiction()['roots'] (artifact.py:101) and tests each rule with artifact._rule_matches(rule, rel) (artifact.py:128), then spells the result as <root>/<under>, <root>/**/<parent> or <root>/**/<name>, or returns None when no rule matches. compile() calls path_class. It does not call artifact.locate(), which answers a different question (root plus rel for an absolute path).
